doc.title: Jerry Gordon interviewed by Monk Rowe and Christian Goodwillie, via Zoom, June 30, 2021

chapter: Teenage obsession and the record store
title: Little Jimmy Scott, the most requested record
summary: The store's most requested record was Jimmy Scott's 'Falling in Love is Wonderful', which he finally obtained and kept rather than sold.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: I would not have guessed that.

Most requested. And here’s a typical conversation. “Hey do you have Jimmy Scott ‘Falling in Love is Wonderful?’” “No, sorry it’s out of print.” “Well could you order it for me? Could you somehow obtain one? Can you copy it for me?” That was the absolute most requested album. I mean other than Stevie Wonder “Songs in the Key of Life” I’m talking about an anomoly okay? And I thought if I ever obtain that record like in a record collection, because that was part of what I did I bought record collections as well. I said if

I ever obtain this record I’m going to get a fortune for it. I am going to gouge them, I’m going to get a fortune for this record. So I don’t know years into my ownership of the record store I got one while obtaining a record collection I couldn’t believe it. Did I sell it? No way. Everybody wanted that record. I kept it, okay? I could have gotten all that money. And that is a — one example of how I learned from my customers, even though I knew plenty of stuff my customers knew more and I learned about what people in the black community wanted and that was a revelation to me and I ate it up.
